Definition: from G1747; to lurk, i.e. (figuratively) plot assassination:--lay wait for.
BiblicalUsage: To lurk, to plot an ambush. Forty men bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink till they had killed Paul in Acts 23:21, and the scribes lay in wait for Jesus, seeking to catch something from His mouth, in Luke 11:54.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ambushers' oath shows how far hatred will go, and the fact that both plots failed shows how far God's protection reaches.
